items.author: 彭海星
items.content: 两天前，代号 PHP2Shell 的两个 PHP 高危远程执行漏洞信息意外泄露，表明在最危险的情况下，攻击者可以通过 PHP 的漏洞，在服务器执行任意代码。 你可能听说过但不熟悉 PHP，但只需要知道， 全世界约有七成网站后台都使用了这项技术 ，使用比例高达 92% 的日本，更是成了「重灾区」。 于是，从昨晚开始，无数网站运维人员经历了夺命连环 call，高市早苗亲自发文敦促网站管理者打补丁，半个欧洲的政府与学术机构紧急「拔网线」，二次元熟悉的 niconico、pixiv，乃至《赛马娘》《碧蓝幻想》和任天堂相关游戏服务也纷纷下线，开始了归期未定的漫长升级。 想象你登录一个电商网站，下单买了一本书。这个过程中你看见的只是前端的网页，但服务器其实在后台处理了诸如验证密码、检查库存、查询订单、生成网页等动态功能。 根据统计，目前有 69.4% 的网站后端用到了 PHP，WordPress、Drupal、Joomla 等流行的网站管理系统都建立在 PHP 之上，维基百科使用的 MediaWiki，同样主要由 PHP 编写。 但就像曾经种满全球的大麦克香蕉被黄叶病团灭一样，普遍性本身也是一种脆弱性：如果 PHP 在底层上出现安全问题，可想而知，几乎全球的网站都会受到牵连。

Zuckerberg said about 25% of people who set up Muse now use it daily, helping improve retention. Recursive , an AI startup founded last year, is starting to live up to its name. The company, which is trying to build AI that can improve itself, released its first model, Flint , on Wednesday. Flint is a free coding model that can run on a laptop and was built largely with the help of AI. Recursive’s automated research system, which it calls the Eureka Machine, helped with nearly every step of Flint’s development, the company says. That let a small team build the model from scratch in under four months. Flint is an early public test of recursive self-improvement: the idea that AI can build better AI, which in turn builds even better AI. It’s also one of the most debated ideas in the industry. Some researchers fear that AI improving itself could slip out of human control. For now, Recursive’s version is more limited: an AI research assistant overseen by people that produced a model small enough for a laptop. The company emerged from stealth in May with $650 million in funding at a $4.65 billion valuation, from backers including GV, Nvidia, and AMD Ventures. Recursive is led by CEO Richard Socher, Salesforce’s former chief scientist.

The U.S. National Security Agency’s sent out an alarming warning on Wednesday that two critical holes had been found in PHP, with patches already issued by the PHP Foundation . PHP is a server-side programming language so widely used for web applications that it powers roughly 70% of the websites on the internet; by some accounts, that’s more than 33 million sites . It is also used by popular content management systems like WordPress. The NSA warned that these holes are so severe that if a website can’t be patched immediately, it should be pulled off the web until it can be. The holes allow attackers to infiltrate the server’s file system or a database that may be used by the web app. Interestingly, these holes have been tucked away in all versions of PHP since version 5, which was released in 2004. Websites not running relatively current versions of PHP will have some updating work to do, as PHP 8.1 and older versions are no longer supported. The recommendation is to update the web server to the current version of PHP, which is 8.5.12.

Companies are giving employees AI tools to make them more productive, but the tools appear to be creating new problems for their managers. More than half of senior leaders say they find it harder to evaluate employees’ work after adopting AI, according to a Nielsen survey of 1,700 directors and senior managers across seven countries, commissioned by work-management company Monday.com. The reason is that much of employees’ output now arrives polished in the manager’s inbox, making it hard to tell how much came from the employee and how much from AI. As a result, nearly half of managers say they spend more time reviewing and guiding their teams’ output than they used to. That’s not to say managers are unhappy about AI. items.description: The proposed policy seems to offer protections against AI running amok but actually forbids federal agencies from blocking a model's release without the permission of a judge.
items.author: Lucas Ropek
items.content: Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now. Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW. Over the past year, concerns have swirled over the potential dangers posed by artificial intelligence, and debates have raged over the proper path for AI safety. Now, Anthropic appears to have put forth its own vision for how the government might regulate its industry. Politico recently reported that the AI lab has been shopping around a new draft bill on AI safety that it hopes Congress might consider adopting. The legislation posits certain scenarios in which the release of an AI model could be blocked from distribution. Those scenarios involve a “foreseeable, imminent risk” — one in which over 50 people are at risk of dying or if over a billion dollars in property damage could result, Politico writes. The catastrophic risk in question must “stem from the creation or release of a biological weapon, the model evading its developer’s controls or a cyberattack,” the outlet notes. The metrics offered here — 50 people and a billion dollars — are similar to those in a piece of California legislation that was recently passed into law, Senate Bill 53 , which similarly defined those scenarios as tantamount to “catastrophic risk.”
